$comment: THE BUNDLED DEFAULT, not the only source. See presets/README.md for the resolution chain:
plugin options -> ~/.config/lacode/pool.json -> this file -> a built-in fallback.
src/lib/pool.ts reads it at config time and rewrites every pooled variant agent
(explore-fast-N, implement-fast-N, context-manager-N) plus the provider whitelists
to match, so no model is written down next to an agent anywhere.
Slot N is the same model for every base agent, which is what makes load shared.
RULES, all validated at startup: models are written provider/model-id, split on the FIRST
slash only so openrouter's vendor-prefixed ids (nvidia/x:free) resolve; must be distinct.
AT MOST 4 SLOTS: one hidden variant per base per slot is declared, so a fifth entry would
route at an agent that does not exist. Extra entries are dropped with a warning.
WEIGHT IS THE ONLY KNOWN KNOB, and it is a SOFT CEILING on how many concurrent claims a
slot holds -- not a share of the work. Priority is that same number, so the rule is:
1. the HIGHEST-weight slot that is still under its ceiling takes the spawn
2. slot 1 therefore fills to its number before slot 2 sees any work at all
3. once EVERY slot is at its ceiling, the overflow goes to the least loaded slot,
so a burst past the summed ceilings degrades to even spreading and never blocks
With this file: longcat (opencode-go) takes 3 sessions to itself, then space-bunny
takes 2, then big-pickle and longcat (Zen) take 1 each -- sequence 1,1,1,2,2,3,4,...
Equal weights give a plain round robin in list order. 2,2,1,1 reproduces the old
primary/overflow cycle exactly, which is why the old tier values still work.
Absent means weight 1. Must be a number in (0, 100]; anything else warns and uses 1.
List order is the tie-break between slots of equal weight, so put the ones you want
first and treat the bottom of the list as the reserve.
COST IS THE POLICY, NOT A CONSTRAINT. These four slots are free because that is what
the pool is FOR: mechanical work -- reading files, grepping, mechanical edits, cartography.
They are not here to be the smartest model in the system. The point of putting that work
on a near-free model is that the mechanical tokens stop being spent by your expensive
main model, and that the main model's context is never filled with file contents it does
not need to reason about. Those are two separate effects and the second is the larger one.
You MAY substitute your own list, including paid models, and nothing will reject it:
no allowlist, no cost filter, no validation beyond structure (US-7). That is a deliberate
override of the default, not a supported alternative to it -- a priced model in the pool
is paying per token for work a free model does well enough, which usually costs more than
it saves. If you do it anyway, that is your call; the plugin will say so once at startup
when it can price the model, and stay silent when it cannot, because it will not guess.
To use your own models, edit the "slots" array below (the one-line edit is: replace a
{"model": ...} entry with your own provider/id and keep the weight) or leave this file
alone entirely and put the list in ~/.config/lacode/pool.json instead, which wins over it.
Re-check any model you substitute against models.dev; the pinned prices this project
refuses to guess live are in tests/models-snapshot.json.
Changing this file requires restarting every opencode process: plugins are not hot-reloaded.
